title: Brexit uncertainty & sterling weakness
summary: Prolonged Brexit negotiations kept sterling volatile through 2019. Since UK pump prices are set in GBP but crude is traded in USD, a weaker pound raises the sterling cost of oil even when the dollar crude price is flat.

title: COVID-19 demand collapse & negative WTI
summary: Global lockdowns from March 2020 caused the sharpest demand collapse in oil market history. Storage capacity nearly ran out and WTI crude briefly traded at a negative price on 20 April 2020. UK pump prices fell to their lowest point in the dataset (petrol ~104.87p) in May 2020 as demand for road fuel evaporated.

title: Saudi-Russia price war
summary: After OPEC+ talks collapsed in early March 2020, Saudi Arabia launched a price war and ramped up output just as COVID demand was collapsing, compounding the crash in crude prices.

title: Demand recovery & fuel duty freeze
summary: As lockdowns eased through 2021, road fuel demand and crude prices climbed steadily back toward pre-pandemic levels. UK fuel duty remained frozen (as it had been since 2011), so the rise over 2021 tracks the underlying wholesale product cost rather than tax changes.

title: Russia's invasion of Ukraine
summary: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022 triggered fears of sanctions on one of the world's largest oil exporters. Brent crude spiked toward $130/bbl in early March, and UK petrol jumped from about 149p to over 159p in a single week (14 March 2022), one of the largest weekly rises in the dataset.

title: UK fuel duty cut by 5p/litre
summary: In response to record pump prices, the UK Spring Statement 2022 cut fuel duty by 5 pence per litre from 23 March 2022, the largest cash-terms cut on record, which is visible as a step down in the duty columns of the dataset.

title: Record UK pump prices
summary: Despite the duty cut, continued supply tightness and a weak pound pushed UK pump prices to record highs in the summer of 2022 - the dataset's all-time peak of 191.55p for petrol falls in this window (early July 2022).

title: OPEC+ production cuts
summary: OPEC+ announced a series of output cuts from October 2022 through 2023 to support prices amid recession fears and falling demand growth, contributing to the choppier, lower-trending prices through late 2022 and 2023 relative to the summer 2022 peak.

title: Israel-Hamas war & Middle East risk premium
summary: The outbreak of the Israel-Hamas war in October 2023 raised concerns about wider Middle East instability and shipping risk, adding a geopolitical risk premium to crude prices through the final quarter of 2023.

title: Red Sea shipping attacks
summary: Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden through early-to-mid 2024 forced vessels onto longer routes around Africa, raising freight and insurance costs that fed through to fuel markets.

title: US-Israel-Iran war & Strait of Hormuz blockade
summary: US and Israeli military operations against Iran began in late February 2026. Iran responded by attacking shipping and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for roughly a fifth of global oil flow. Brent crude surged over 50% in March 2026 alone, one of the steepest monthly rallies on record, briefly nearing $120/bbl. Prices whipsawed through the following months on ceasefire talks, renewed strikes and reports of the US considering direct military action to reopen the Strait - each swing visible as sharp weekly moves in the dataset from March through August 2026.
